content.text:
I submitted **index 25 (Cr 0.16, Sb 0.84)** as the best composition. It had the highest efficiency of the three I measured: **0.122% EQE** (external quantum efficiency, the merit named for this library).

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 13 | 0.49 | 0.0087 |
| 22 | 0.77 | 0.101 |
| 25 | 0.84 | **0.122** |

- **Why I started at index 13:** the models picked out CrSbO₄ (Cr:Sb 1:1) as the most promising phase. It came out nearly stable (0.065 eV/atom above the hull) with a predicted band gap of about 2.0 eV, so it should absorb the 3.2 eV light. The measurement was poor anyway: 0.0087%.
- **Why I moved to the Sb-rich end:** the model predictions didn't explain the results, so after the first measurement I chose where to measure from the EQE trend. EQE rose more than tenfold between Sb 0.49 and Sb 0.77, and rose again at Sb 0.84.

**Limits of this result:**
- The Sb-rich end is not settled. EQE was still rising at index 25, so indices 26–27 (Sb 0.86–0.87) could be better, and I had no measurements left to check them.
- The Cr-rich side (indices 0–10) was never measured. I ruled it out only because EQE fell so steeply toward the 1:1 composition.
- None of the 5 XRD scans were used, so I don't know which crystal phases are actually present in the films.
